narrative:
Your application was denied because the prediction estimated an 83% probability that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. This is a high-risk estimate, not a certainty, but it was strong enough to drive the rejection.

The most important factor was your part-time enrollment status. Among accepted students, nearly all studied full-time (92.8%), while part-time study was rare (7.2%). In your case, being part-time was the strongest push toward the failure prediction. The second most important factor was your third-year class standing: your decile of 3 was well below the accepted-student average of 5.79, and this lower standing also pushed toward failure. Your middle-income family bracket had the smallest influence among the top three; it leaned toward failure but was far less decisive, especially since middle-income students make up a substantial share of accepted applicants. All three top factors worked against you.

To improve your chances, ask admissions what evidence would strengthen a reapplication. Consider moving to full-time study if feasible, and provide context about why you studied part-time and what support systems you would use. You should also strengthen evidence of academic readiness, particularly upper-year performance, and consider retaking the LSAT or completing additional coursework before reapplying.
